item.title: Mad about mara: the DIY dance movement helping young Nigerians escape the daily grind
item.description:
What started as one artist’s response to being cut out of a music video has exploded, becoming a driving force in Nigeria’s cultural landscape

As a student in the central Nigerian city of Ilorin, Lawal Habeeb Kola loved staying in his hostel room to produce beats rather than returning to his family house in Lagos, the more frenetic city of his birth.

In 2022, one of his beats became popular on TikTok, and a version featuring ad-libbed vocals from a hypeman sent it viral. He was invited to the music video shoot in Lagos and thought his big break had finally come, but when the video was released, he was absent.

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Eromo Egbejule in Lagos

item.title: ‘I’m no longer a UAE official’: UN hopeful Lana Nusseibeh tries to shake off Sudan record
item.description:
The US and Russia’s candidate for secretary general is on a charm offensive. Can she overcome London’s resistance to her bid?

Lana Nusseibeh is in Britain this week, attempting to present herself as a potential future UN secretary general, and shift the focus from her past as a United Arab Emirates diplomat who denied the country’s role in arming a militia accused of war crimes and genocide in Sudan’s four-year civil war.

It is a high-risk strategy that involves meeting ministers, MPs, academics and holding a public event with the UN Association.

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor

item.title: At least 31 killed as fuel tanker crash ignites large fire on Cairo highway
item.description:
Blaze on ring road surrounding Egyptian capital injures at least 21 people and leaves cars and motorcycles charred

A crash involving a fuel tanker ignited a huge fire on a highway surrounding Cairo on Wednesday, killing at least 31 people, Egyptian authorities said.

The blaze on the ring road, a key artery that encircles the Egyptian capital, also injured at least 21 people and left more than two dozen cars and motorcycles charred, according to the latest figures released by the health ministry.

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Associated Press

item.title: Swiss tourist killed and British and Americans injured by elephants in Cameroon
item.description:
Alain Throo, insurance executive based in London, reportedly gored and later died on hike near Mount Cameroon national park

A Swiss tourist has been killed and British and American tourists have been injured when a group of hikers encountered a herd of elephants in Cameroon.

The group of six tourists, four British, one Swiss and one American, accompanied by local guides, were hiking near the village of Bakingili in the south of the Mount Cameroon national park on 19 November, on a path used by elephants to access a nearby lake, when they encountered the herd of about 15 animals, according to media reports.

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Rachel Savage in Johannesburg

item.title: Sri Lankan asylum seeker killed himself after being sent by UK to Eswatini
item.description:
Kishanth Peramalya was denied entry due to sexual assault convictions and sent to Africa where he had no connections

The UK sent a Sri Lankan asylum seeker who had been convicted of sexual assault to Eswatini, a southern African country to which he had no connection and where he killed himself.

Kishanth Peramalya was part of a group that set sail from India hoping to reach Canada and claim asylum there. The boat was rescued by the Royal Navy in October 2021 when it got into difficulty and brought to Diego Garcia in the remote British Indian Ocean Territory, which hosts a US-UK military base.

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Rachel Savage in Johannesburg

item.title: All hostages rescued after Colombian security forces storm supermarket, police say
item.description:
Unclear if ‘hostage-taker’ who was killed may have been a hostage as daylong siege in Cartagena shopping centre ends

Colombian police have stormed a supermarket in one of the country’s most popular tourist cities, ending a daylong siege in which all the hostages were freed and one man police described as a hostage-taker was killed.

Abelardo de la Espriella, the far-right president, travelled to the Caribbean port city of Cartagena to follow the final hours of negotiations and the tactical assault, in which special forces officers broke through blocked entrances and detonated stun grenades.

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Tiago Rogero South America correspondent

item.title: Lululemon founder stuns Canadian women’s leadership conference with sexist comments
item.description:
Chip Wilson said men importing brides from Thailand was due to women waiting too long to have children

The controversial founder of Lululemon suggested women in Canada are having too few children and this could lead some men to bring in brides from Thailand, in remarks that stunned audience members at a women’s leadership conference.

Chip Wilson, who built the Vancouver yoga-wear startup into a global athleisure empire, was a featured speaker at the Leadership Forum in Calgary earlier this week, an event organized by Axis Connects to advance women in leadership. The organization says it aims to create space for “candid conversations about the barriers women face both in business and society”.

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Leyland Cecco in Toronto

item.title: Colombia’s president arrives at scene of supermarket hostage siege in tourist city
item.description:
Abelardo de la Espriella to take control of operation trying to free at least 20 hostages

Colombia’s president has arrived at the scene of an hours-long standoff between security services and gunmen holding at least 20 people hostage inside a supermarket in Cartagena, a popular tourist city.

Abelardo de la Espriella’s motorcade arrived in Cartagena on Tuesday night, Agence France-Presse reported, where he will ostensibly take control of an operation involving scores of officers, the navy and special forces.

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Tiago Rogero, South America correspondent, and agencies

item.title: Kilmar Ábrego García, man at center of Trump deportation battle, leaves US
item.description:
Salvadorian man, who was deported in March 2025 and returned to US after supreme court ruling, leaving of own volition for Spain

Kilmar Ábrego García has left the United States of his own volition, his lawyers confirmed on Tuesday, with the Department of Homeland Security confirming that he was travelling to Spain.

A source close to Ábrego said Madrid was his first stop but that it would not be his final destination.

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Cris Seda Chabrier in New York

item.title: Canada says it ‘does not report to the US’ after Pentagon criticizes military spending
item.description:
Scathing US document memo supposedly ‘atrophied’ defence capabilities of its northern neighbour

Canada is a “sovereign nation” that does not “report” to the United States, the country’s defense minister said after the Pentagon released a scathing memo that criticized the supposedly “atrophied” defence capabilities of its northern neighbour.

The document, released on Tuesday, said Canada had “yet to make the hard decisions and tradeoffs” necessary to meet previous defence spending pledges and become a “credible partner in the defense of our shared continent”.

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Leyland Cecco in Toronto

item.title: New Zealand election: final results show ruling coalition needs minor party to govern
item.description:
Incumbent prime minister Christopher Luxon loses majority and needs support of Opportunity party to remain in power, or country faces another election

The final results of New Zealand’s general election show the incumbent rightwing coalition will need the support of a centrist newcomer party to form a government, and to avoid sending the country back to the polls.

Preliminary results on 7 November handed the National party and its two coalition partners, the populist New Zealand First and libertarian Act parties, a slim two-seat majority, making the election too close to call until final votes were tallied.

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Eva Corlett in Wellington

item.title: Threat from China looms large over Taiwan’s local elections
item.description:
Taiwanese officials raise alarm over interference by China in elections that will shape fortunes of ruling party

Taiwanese voters go to the polls on Saturday in closely watched local elections that will shape the fortunes of the ruling Democratic Progressive party (DPP) as it navigates an increasingly precarious set of relationships on the global stage.

Saturday’s vote will choose mayors, council members and other local leaders across 22 districts. Unlike the presidential elections, in which foreign policy is often a key issue, the local elections, held every four years, are largely focused on bread-and-butter issues such as housing affordability and wealth distribution.

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Amy Hawkins and Yu-chen Li in Taipei

item.title: China reserves right to take ‘necessary measures’ after Trump’s new tariff proposals
item.description:
Beijing says new levies amount to ‘political manipulation’, while Brazil ‘will not yield to this type of threat’

  • Trump proposing new tariffs on 14 partners including China and EU

Beijing has said it reserves the right to take “necessary measures” after Donald Trump’s administration proposed new tariffs on goods from China and other major trading partners, triggering a global backlash.

Among the suggested levies on 14 major trading partners announced on Wednesday, China is potentially facing one of the biggest hits. It would face the highest capped rate of 20%, which in some cases will be stacked on top of other import taxes for a total rate of 45%.

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Bailey and agencies

item.title: ‘Trapped in grief’: wife of Japanese journalist detained by Russia pleads for his release
item.description:
Yuki Imai being held in Moscow on allegations he conducted ‘espionage’ while working for a newspaper in Sakhalin island in Russia’s far east

The wife of a Japanese journalist who has been detained in Russia for more than a month on suspicion of spying has issued an emotive appeal for his release.

Yuki Imai, a reporter for the Hokkaido Shimbun, was arrested in mid-October as he was preparing to return to Japan from a two-year assignment at the Japanese newspaper’s bureau in the city of Yuzhno-Sakhalinsk, on the island of Sakhalin in Russia’s far east.

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Justin McCurry in Tokyo

item.title: China sends first foreign astronaut to ISS rival as it globalises space operations
item.description:
Muhammad Zeeshan Ali – the first Pakistani to reach orbit – greeted with Chinese ‘space handshake’ at Tiangong station

China has flown the first foreign astronaut to its Tiangong space station, starting what it says will be the globalisation of its space operations as the US-led International Space Station (ISS) enters its final years of operation.

Floating through a hatch to enter Tiangong, Pakistan’s Muhammad Zeeshan Ali grinned broadly as he was embraced by the onboard crew in what China’s space agency called the country’s first foreign “space handshake”.

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Bailey and agencies

item.title: Jess Wilson’s plan for Melbourne sewage plants risks water and wetlands without bringing debt down, experts say
item.description:
Academic says Victorian Liberal proposal to lease treatment plants and generate profit with no compromise of services ‘a total furphy’

  • Victorian election 2026 guide: what you need to know

  • Confused about who to vote for? Check the parties’ key promises and policies

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

Experts have warned the Victorian Liberals’ plan to lease Melbourne’s sewage treatment plants is a “smoke and mirrors” way to pay off debt that risks compromising the state’s water resources and crucial wetlands for nearly a century.

On Thursday – two days out from the election – the opposition leader, Jess Wilson, announced plans for a 90-year lease of the Eastern and Western treatment plants, which process the vast majority of the city’s sewage and are run by Melbourne Water.

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Josh Taylor

item.title: Labor faces prospect of electoral wipeout in Victoria as voters turn to Liberals and One Nation
item.description:
Former ALP strategist says Ben Carroll government at risk of losing more than 30 seats in Saturday’s election, to fall behind Pauline Hanson’s party

  • Victorian election 2026 guide: what you need to know

  • Confused about who to vote for? Check the parties’ key promises and policies

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

The Victorian Labor government is facing an electoral wipeout after 12 years in office as the state heads to the polls on Saturday.

Polling during the campaign has consistently pointed to a Coalition victory. The final Newspoll, released on Thursday, showed the Coalition 15 points ahead on a two-party-preferred basis.

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Benita Kolovos Victorian state correspondent

item.title: NSW Labor is ‘trampling over party principles’ with preselections by captain’s call, members say
item.description:
Exclusive: Ryde councillor Penny Pedersen was asked by Labor head office not to nominate for Lane Cove in March state election

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Labor’s New South Wales leadership has been accused of alienating members and undermining the democratic process, after multiple state election candidates were preselected by “captain’s call” instead of the rank and file.

The premier, Chris Minns, announced on Friday that commercial litigator Jade Tyrrell will be Labor’s candidate for the marginal Liberal-held seat of Lane Cove at March’s state election.

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Penry Buckley NSW state reporter

item.title: ‘Crisis in empathy’: prison guard was watching TV while Aboriginal man was dying in custody, NSW coroner finds
item.description:
Judge says officers should be banned from screens and phones while on shift after the 33-year-old’s death at Silverwater

• Warning: This article contains references to Indigenous Australians who have died

The NSW coroner has found the death of an Aboriginal man in custody in 2023 was not only preventable but was “one of the most egregious deaths” she had investigated.

Corrective Services NSW has been recommended to overhaul officer training for self-harm responses, and ban officers’ access to TV and YouTube while on shift.

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Josh Taylor and Douglas Smith

item.title: Grace Tame calls out ex-Murdoch media executive who said she ‘must be looking to be raped again’
item.description:
Matt Handbury, nephew of Rupert Murdoch, admits making offensive remark and says he was referencing assault survivor’s ‘strikingly attractive get-up’

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A former Murdoch media executive has admitted he said Grace Tame “must be looking to be raped again” at an event, after the former Australian of the year overheard the comment and confronted him.

Tame, a child sexual assault victim survivor who was Australian of the year in 2021 for her advocacy work, revealed in an opinion piece for Crikey that she heard Matt Handbury make the comment to another man at a function last week.

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Jordyn Beazley

item.title: Spanish prime minister Pedro Sánchez confident of election victory despite polls – Europe live
item.description:
‘I can’t conceive of us losing,’ the leader said

Freelance journalist based in Madrid and host of the Sobremesa podcast

Vox has often been portrayed in international coverage as a party of Franco nostalgists whose ultraconservative Catholicism and civil-war rhetoric towards the separatist Catalan “enemy within” threatened a return to the worst of Spain’s recent past.

item.title: King tides batter US coasts as storms threaten Thanksgiving celebrations
item.description:
Heavy rain, strong winds and coastal flooding creating hazardous conditions for millions travelling for holiday

King tides and huge waves have been battering both coasts of the US during a turbulent Thanksgiving period, with severe weather threatening millions across the country. Along the California coast, king tides caused considerable damage. In Pacifica, south of San Francisco, large waves battered the coastline on Wednesday, destroying part of a pier and sending debris into the ocean.

The National Weather Service issued coastal flood warnings covering parts of the Pacific coastline and shorelines around San Francisco Bay and San Pablo Bay. Several beachfront properties in Pacifica have already experienced flooding, while authorities in Marin County temporarily issued an evacuation warning for residents of beachfront homes at Stinson Beach.

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Matt Andrews

item.title: French town divided over church bells ringing every 15 minutes at night
item.description:
Longtime residents of La Garnache defeat newer neighbours in latest rural culture clash over ‘sensory heritage’

A ding-dong has divided the town of La Garnache in western France over attempts to silence the bells of the local church, which strike all night.

Since 1942, the clock tower of Notre-Dame de l’Assomption has chimed an eighth-century hymn every 15 minutes … day and night. Between 10pm and 7am, the bells ring 37 times, adding up to more than 700 individual chimes.

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Kim Willsher

item.title: At critical juncture, Friedrich Merz finds Germans’ support for Ukraine wavering
item.description:
German chancellor is on difficult terrain, at home and abroad, as he fights to maintain European backing for Kyiv

The German chancellor, Friedrich Merz, is navigating choppy waters both at home and abroad over his insistence that Europe must keep up support – both military and financial – for Ukraine.

At a Brussels summit on Thursday, Merz reiterated his view that all EU member states – pointedly, “not 23 or 24” – should support a €45bn (£38bn) loan for Ukraine for 2027. He has threatened to veto the bloc’s budget unless all countries sign up to the loan, a stance that saw him accused of “classic blackmail” by Robert Fico, the populist prime minister of Slovakia. Czechia, Hungary and Bulgaria have also voiced their misgivings, to varying degrees, over Berlin’s dogged position.

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Kate Connolly in Berlin

item.title: Race hate exploded in this Spanish town last year. Now its residents are bracing for more
item.description:
Torre-Pacheco’s diverse communities are fearful that the far-right Vox party will enter government after Sunday’s election

Sitting on a park bench, taking in the sunny day, Naima reflected on all that had seemingly changed since she moved to Spain three decades earlier.

Back then, the Moroccan national had felt warmly welcomed by Spaniards. “I had never, at any point in my life, felt like there was racism,” she said. “But now things are changing. And the blame lies with rightwing politics.”

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Ashifa Kassam in Torre-Pacheco, Murcia

item.title: Momentous decision looms after judges call for Netanyahu charges to be dropped
item.description:
Dropping of corruption charges against Israeli PM after unusual intervention could set damaging precedent

The Israeli judges presiding over Benjamin Netanyahu’s corruption trial have called on prosecutors to end proceedings, a highly unusual intervention that leaves the attorney general facing a momentous political decision.

The prime minister has been charged with bribery, fraud and breach of trust in three complex and overlapping criminal cases that hinge on his relationship with telecoms magnates and other wealthy businessmen. Ending the trial without a ruling could set damaging precedents for media independence and how politicians are held to account.

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Emma Graham-Harrison in Jerusalem

item.title: Israeli strikes kill 16 schoolchildren so far this month, Gaza ministry says
item.description:
Statement follows death of sisters, aged 15 and 13, in airstrike on residential apartment in Gaza City

Israeli strikes have killed at least 16 schoolchildren in Gaza since the start of November, as young people across the territory face intensifying bombardment and a struggle to find food, clean water and shelter.

On Wednesday, Gaza’s ministry of education said: “Palestinian students had been targeted for the third time in less than 24 hours, in an escalation reflecting the continued Israeli violations against children in the Gaza Strip. The number of schoolchildren killed since the beginning of November has now risen to 16.”

Continue reading...

item.title: Israel ‘officially sanctions’ torture of Palestinian prisoners to extract confessions, report concludes
item.description:
Public Committee Against Torture in Israel examined 42 complaints against Shin Bet interrogators over past decade

Israel has institutionalised the use of torture to extract confessions from Palestinian prisoners, sometimes documenting abuse in official records or granting advanced approval for “special measures” in interrogation, according to a report from the Public Committee Against Torture in Israel (PCATI).

This dangerous practice risked leading to irreversible miscarriages of justice, as Israel moved to implement a racist new death penalty law that targets Palestinians, the report said.

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Emma Graham-Harrison and Lorenzo Tondo in Jerusalem

item.title: UN sacked Palestinian staff on back of unproven Israeli allegations, tribunal rules
item.description:
Judgment casts doubt on evidence linking aid workers to Hamas and says humanitarian efforts in Gaza were damaged

A UN tribunal has cast doubt on the evidence used to justify the sacking of Palestinian UN aid workers in 2024, saying it was based “almost entirely” on unproven assertions from the Israeli government and had damaged humanitarian operations in Gaza.

The judgment, seen by the Guardian, raises fresh questions about the decision by the UN Relief and Works Agency (Unrwa), the main humanitarian organisation working in Gaza, to sack members of staff. It was taken on the basis of Israeli allegations of involvement in the Hamas-led attacks of 7 October 2023.

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Julian Borger Senior international correspondent

item.title: Palestinian journalist killed by Israel in Gaza wins Rory Peck prize
item.description:
Mariam Dagga shares award with two of her colleagues from AP for ‘powerful coverage’ of human cost of war

Mariam Dagga, the Palestinian war correspondent who was killed at the age of 33 in Gaza in an Israeli strike, has posthumously won the prestigious Rory Peck prize for freelance video journalists, the organisers announced on Wednesday.

She shares the award with two of her colleagues from the Associated Press (AP), Abdel Kareem Hana and Jehad Alshrafi, “for their powerful coverage of the human cost of the war” in the Palestinian territory, the Rory Peck Trust said.

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Nadeem Badshah

item.title: Oxford museum displays seized belongings of Naga freedom fighter Gaidinliu for first time
item.description:
Notebooks, clothes and ritual objects taken by British forces in India in the 1930s go on show at Pitt Rivers Museum

In 1932, British forces in north-east India imprisoned a 17-year-old girl called Gaidinliu for leading an uprising against colonial rule. While pursuing the freedom fighter through hills and valleys in the homeland of the Naga people, colonial officers also seized some of her most treasured possessions.

They were sent to the University of Oxford’s Pitt Rivers Museum and kept in storage. Now, for the first time, the museum is exhibiting the collection of 27 items, including a basket of Gaidinliu’s notebooks believed to contain her prophetic visions as the leader of a Naga Indigenous religion, clothes, bracelets and amulets.

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: David Batty

item.title: Politician hosts 400,000 guests at daughter’s wedding in India’s poorest state
item.description:
Six helipads built and feast prepared by 500 cooks for wedding hosted by Anant Singh, an MP charged with murder

It takes a brave soul to try to match the mythic opulence of the wedding arranged by the Indian billionaire Mukesh Ambani for his son Anant in 2024. Estimates of the cost for the months-long celebration ran to at least $600m, with world leaders and celebrities among those on the guest list.

Smaller fry though he is, Anant Singh, a legislator in India’s poorest state, Bihar, gave it his best shot on Wednesday, albeit in a rustic rural setting, for the nuptials of his daughter Shivangi Singh, and Rishikesh Kumar, an MBA student from Georgia State University in Atlanta.

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Amrit Dhillon in Delhi

item.title: Indian Cockroach movement leader asks court for permission to fly to UK
item.description:
Officials at Delhi airport stopped Saurav Das from boarding flight to Britain, where students have invited him to speak

A leader of India’s youth-led Cockroach movement has asked the Delhi high court to give him permission to fly to the UK after immigration officials at Delhi airport stopped him boarding a flight early on Tuesday morning.

The court is scheduled to hear Saurav Das’s case on Thursday morning. His lawyer asked the court for a quick hearing because Das has by now already missed some of his engagements at British universities and can only attend the other events on his itinerary if he is allowed to fly out as soon as possible.

item.dc:creator: Amrit Dhillon in Delhi

item.title: World Chess Championship 2026 Game 1: Gukesh Dommaraju and Javokhir Sindarov play to 38-move draw – as it happened
item.description:
• Sindarov and Gukesh play to 38-move draw in Game 1

  • Explainer: all your pre-match questions, answered

  • Sindarov interview: ‘I can’t play games just for fun’

  • Play through 22 famous world championship games

The players have shaken hands and we’re off! We have a Berlin defense of the Ruy Lopez (1 e4 e5 2 Nf3 Nc6 3 Bb5 Nf6), one of the most thoroughly analyzed openings in modern chess.

The Berlin famously helped Vladimir Kramnik dethrone Garry Kasparov in their 2000 world title match in London and has been a staple of elite chess ever since, earning a reputation as one of black’s most reliable weapons against 1 e4.

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Bryan Armen Graham

item.title: Leader of India’s Cockroach movement says he was stopped from boarding flight to UK
item.description:
Saurav Das was due to give talks at UK universities on protest movement but says ‘coward government’ prevented him flying

A leader of India’s youth-led Cockroach movement has said he was prevented from leaving Delhi to fly to the UK to give talks on the viral group’s protests.

Saurav Das, 27, has been at the forefront of the Cockroach Janta party (CJP), which has amassed millions of social media followers since its launch in May. Das, who was due to fly out early on Tuesday, said immigration officials told him at the airport that his passport had been flagged.

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Agence France-Presse in Delhi

item.title: DWP ‘cyber incident’ knocks almost all pensions and benefits systems offline
item.description:
Department for Work and Pensions officials say welfare payments will continue to be made despite huge outage

  • Tell us: have you been affected by the DWP ‘cyber incident’

Almost all pensions and benefits systems in the UK are unavailable after a “cyber incident”.

Anyone trying to check their state pension, make an application for disability benefits or claim universal credit was not able to do so on Friday morning.

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Ben Quinn and Kiran Stacey

item.title: UK pensions department hit by ‘serious cyber incident’, minister says – UK politics live
item.description:
Pat McFadden says the government doesn’t believe any personal data has been compromised

  • Tell us: have you been affected by the DWP ‘cyber incident’

According to Downdetector, which tracks online service outages, reports of problems with the government website appeared to begin last night and peaked at about 8am this morning.

Tory MP Neil Shastri-Hurst has also commented on the disruption at the DWP, saying the incident highlights the importance of protecting essential public services and ensuring they can recover quickly when systems fail.

Today’s cyber incident at DWP is a stark reminder that national resilience is not a tomorrow issue. It means protecting the essential services people rely on every day, with secure systems and the ability to recover quickly when things go wrong.”

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Taz Ali (now) and Tom Ambrose (earlier)

item.title: UK’s taste for cow’s milk sours as sales hit record low
item.description:
Environmental and animal welfare concerns, and taste preferences, are behind rising popularity of vegan alternatives

Has milk gotta lotta bottle? It may not have as much as it used to, with official data showing Britons are buying less cow’s milk than at any point since records began.

Guardian analysis of the government’s family food survey shows the average person bought 1.8 pints (1,024ml) of cow’s milk a week in 2024-25 – the lowest level in the record’s 52-year history and less than half the amount of milk bought in 1974.

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Matthew Pearce

item.title: Antisemitism adviser to launch inquiry into ‘hostile work environment’ at BBC
item.description:
John Mann says he is conducting review after hearing ‘disturbing’ accounts of discrimination from Jewish staff

  • UK politics live – latest updates

The government’s independent adviser on antisemitism has said he is launching an investigation into the BBC after hearing “disturbing” accounts from Jewish staff of discrimination against them.

John Mann, the Labour peer and former MP, said BBC whistleblowers had told him they faced a “hostile work environment” at the broadcaster and that his previous warnings to its management had gone unheeded.

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Michael Savage Media editor

item.title: Meta whistleblower calls on Burnham to go further with ban on NDAs
item.description:
Sarah Wynn-Williams says tech insiders with concerns about AI are being silenced in system reminiscent of George Orwell’s 1984

The Meta whistleblower who made allegations about the social media company’s treatment of teenagers has urged Andy Burnham to go further in banning non-disclosure agreements, warning that tech insiders with concerns about AI development need to be protected.

Sarah Wynn-Williams, who served as the director of global public policy at Meta, then called Facebook, has been unable to talk about a series of allegations made in her memoir as a result of restrictions secured by the company.

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Michael Savage Media editor

item.title: Thanksgiving meal in Florida leads to ‘mass casualty’ food poisoning incident
item.description:
Local media reported that 18 people fell ill after attending a Thanksgiving lunch at a medical center headquarters

A Thanksgiving meal in Florida triggered a bout of food poisoning so bad that local emergency officials said it was a “mass casualty” event as numerous stricken diners were sent to hospital.

Local media reported that 18 people at the Leon Medical Center headquarters in Doral fell ill due to possible food poisoning after attending the center’s annual Thanksgiving lunch on Wednesday.

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Guardian staff

item.title: Bigfoot enthusiasts hope government’s US sightings files are ‘just the beginning’ of proving the creature real
item.description:
The Forest Service’s work will ‘help normalize’ talk happening ‘for decades’, says ‘wood ape’ conservancy director

When the Forest Service, one of the US government’s less sexy departments, quietly posted three documents to its website in mid-October, it was probably hoping to avoid a fuss.

It didn’t succeed. The files were about Bigfoot, after all, and their publication sparked interest from around the globe, with Bigfoot enthusiasts hopeful that this could be a key step step in the road to proving the creature is real.

item.title: Trump Medicaid cuts will hit the most vulnerable Americans, officials say
item.description:
In Kentucky, one of America’s unhealthiest states, denial of healthcare and potential closure of hospitals may affect 250,000 people

The coalfields of eastern Kentucky fueled America’s economic rise in the early 20th century. But the state has since found itself left behind. A lack of investments in rural regions has triggered health and socioeconomic issues that have lingered for generations.

Today, Kentucky faces the third-highest cancer and third-highest drug overdose death rate in the country and is one of the top five worst-affected states in several other health metrics. It has come to rely heavily on federal healthcare assistance, with about 1.4 million people in Kentucky receiving Medicaid support.

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Stephen Starr in Covington, Kentucky

item.title: Trump claims revised economic data shows pre-midterms figures were ‘fake’ | First Thing
item.description:
President calls for investigation after GDP figures were adjusted upwards, despite revisions to official economic figures being commonplace. Plus, the weird and macabre world of Victorian Christmas cards

  • Don’t already get First Thing in your inbox? Sign up here

Good morning. Donald Trump has alleged without evidence that economic figures published by the US federal government before this month’s midterm elections were “fake” and demanded an investigation after voters roundly rejected his Republican party.

In a holiday message on his Truth Social platform, the US president wished a happy Thanksgiving “to even those who issued fake Economic Numbers, just prior to the Election, and corrected them yesterday, three weeks late, showing that the GDP was actually 4.3%, versus 3.4%”.

Why did Trump call the figures fake? Revisions to official economic figures are commonplace, but Trump has tried repeatedly to challenge trust in economic data that does not support his claims that a historic boom is under way in the US. “Why wasn’t the correct number issued before the Election? I am asking for an immediate investigation of this situation,” Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform. “This is not a small error, this is a massive, and purposeful, error”.

What other acerbic well-wishes did Trump offer? He wished “a very Happy Thanksgiving to all of those people that have worked so hard to bring our Country to the Radical Far Left” as well as “those who want to redistribute Property, so that all of the hardworking people that have built up, over a lifetime, a certain Wealth, will now be forced to distribute it throughout the Country, even to those who refuse to work”.

Why are the ballots at the center of an ongoing dispute over the 2020 election? Some Republicans, led by Trump, claimed the election results had been rigged despite Joe Biden being certified after several recounts. Republican state officials had refused to overturn the result, despite a now-infamous phone call from Trump to pressure the Georgia secretary of state, Brad Raffensperger, to “find 11,780 votes”.

item.title: ‘It’s not helping’: calls for guardrails and regulations as AI use rises at US retailers
item.description:
Labor leaders and advocates urge protections for workers and consumers as AI use becomes more commonplace

As millions of Americans begin holiday shopping this Black Friday, consumers and workers alike are already seeing how artificial intelligence is reshaping the retail landscape.

Anna, a cashier in a southern Oregon Walmart and leader with United for Respect, who requested to remain anonymous for fear of retaliation, criticized the implementation of AI at Walmart and its effects on workers.
